description: Team Breathe is a solo R&D initiative led by Remi Olaiya (Thohat Ventures), bridging biophysical mathematics, edge mobile architecture, and zero-knowledge data verification. Team Breathe delivers real-time predictive autonomic telemetry to eliminate clinical diagnostic lag for astronauts on lunar and Martian missions.
summary:
Sentinel Settle is an edge computed biophysical shield born from neurodivergent sensory overload prevention, where noisy baselines, rapid escalation, and false alarms - that trigger the spiral - forced a new detector. 

Instead of slow RMSSD averages, it measures Ω_cal — the autonomic shear displaced from each crew member’s own first 30 beats and is gated by a 4-second, 5-beat tactical filter. On 256 Hz NASA Langley flight-crew ECG under a strict 3-minute scoring window, it caught 18/19 high-workload events at 0.07 (19/19 at 0.19) versus 8/19 for RMSSD, delivering up to 678 seconds (11.3 minutes) of early warning on the LOFT scenario and holding up under Leave-One-Scenario-Out testing. 

Built for 22-minute deep-space latency, it pairs early detection with Breath Sanctuary haptic pacing (designed, awaiting clinical proof) and zero-PII flight-surgeon bundles for asynchronous Earth downlink.
details:
Origin & The Deep-Space Operational Gap

This architecture began where failure is fastest: preventing acute sensory and cognitive overload in neurodivergent people.

Autonomic baselines are noisy. Escalation is rapid. And a false alarm causes the spiral you’re trying to prevent.

That forced us to abandon slow, windowed HRV averages like RMSSD — they detect overload after performance has already degraded — and build a stateless kinematic shear detector: Ω_cal, re-anchored to each person’s own first 30 beats and gated by a 5-beat (~4-second) tactical gasket.

In deep space, that discipline becomes mission critical. On Artemis and Mars transit, one-way latency hits 22 minutes. No cloud. No real time flight surgeon. The crew needs an onboard safeguard that sees thinning before failure, without crying wolf.

That’s what Sentinel Settle was built for.

How Sentinel Settle Works

Sentinel Settle is a local-first autonomic workload and cognitive-overload early-warning system powered by a Scale-Invariant Kinematic Engine:

1. Measurements in Space: Ingests raw beat-to-beat R-R intervals via standard Bluetooth Low Energy GATT profiles (0x180D/0x2A37), compatible with flight proven chest straps without EEG scalp caps or fixed cockpit cameras.

2. Kinematics & Baseline Re-Anchoring: After session baseline re-anchoring (Ω_cal), the engine computes finite-difference velocity and acceleration across bilaterally clamped intervals (Δτ ∈ [0.01 s, 5.0 s]) and decomposes instantaneous acceleration into tangential physical exertion (a∥) versus transverse orthogonal shear (a⊥),. Integrating |a⊥| over a 30-beat ring buffer (Fc) yields a real-time State Uncertainty Coordinate (Ω_cal) bounded by Metastable Thinning (Ω ≥ 0.07) and Phase Veto (Ω ≥ 0.19).

3. Two-Tier Alarm Philosophy & Crew Action:

Nominal (Ω < 0.07): Silent monitoring; zero crew interruption.

Metastable Thinning (0.07 ≤ Ω < 0.19, sustained ≥ Tier-1 ~4 s tactical / Tier-2 15 min habitat gasket): Low-arousal cue routing the astronaut into the Breath Sanctuary —designed for closed-loop, eyes-closed tactile haptic pacing to support autonomic recovery without habitat disruption.

Phase Veto (Ω ≥ 0.19): High-priority workload redline alert to pause non critical checklist items and serialie local SQLite telemetry into a zero-PII Asynchronous Flight Surgeon Telemetry Bundle (.json) for delayed Earth downlink.

NASA Open Data & Empirical Validation

This mission architecture is anchored to two official NASA Human Research Roadmap challenge resources — Risk of Inadequate Systems Operations Support and Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders — which define the operational risk of unmonitored crew cognitive overload under delayed ground communications. We validated `src/nasa_omega_validator.py` across two open-access NASA datasets:

NASA Langley Flight Crew Physiological Data (`25.zip`, 1.31 h pooled 256 Hz ECG across CA, DA, LOFT, SS): Detected a 677.7-second (~11.3-minute) metastable thinning lead time on 25_LOFT prior to the labeled workload event.

Across 19 ground-truth Event episodes under a strict 180-second tactical horizon (with our Tier-1 5-beat / ~3.99 s sustained gasket), pooled Ω_cal achieved 18/19 (94.7%) event recall at Ω ≥ 0.07 (0.639 precision, 22.97 FA/h) and 19/19 (100%) event recall at Ω ≥ 0.19 (0.587 precision, 19.90 FA/h) — outperforming both standard rolling RMSSD drop (8/19 recall, 0.625 precision) and HR +10 bpm (13/19 recall, 0.761 precision).

In 4-fold Leave-One-Scenario-Out (LOSO) hold-out testing with LOFT completely withheld, fixed 0.07/0.19 thresholds achieved 5/6 event recall (677.7 s lead time), while out-of-sample Youden-fit thresholds achieved 6/6 recall (590.1 s lead time).

Under a 900 s mission horizon, gasketed false alarms drop to 0.00/h (1.000 precision).

NASA OSDR Study OSD-575 (SpaceX Inspiration4, N = 4 discrete serum panels): Evaluated 9-biomarker state vector displacement across 28 pre/post-flight crew timepoints (L- vs. R+) as supporting multi-biomarker evidence, achieving 1.000 sensitivity and 1.000 specificity at the Ω ≥ 0.19 Phase Veto boundary across all four crew subjects (C001–C004).

Validation Scope, Limitations & Prospective Roadmap ("What's Next")

Current Scope: Early proof-of-concept validated on 1.31 hours of Langley flight-crew telemetry and N = 4 Inspiration4 profiles; longer prospective validation across more crew and mission conditions is required before operational deployment. Closed-loop haptic pacing in Breath Sanctuary is an architectural design pending controlled efficacy trials.

Next Milestone: Prospective multi-crew trials in NASA HERA (Human Exploration Research Analog) isolation campaigns and 6° Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest (HDBR) studies, measuring closed-loop Ω_cal reduction and recovery slope (ΔΩ/Δt) under Breath Sanctuary haptic pacing alongside edge battery/latency profiling on radiation-tolerant BLE hardware.

Prior Work, Open Resources & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

Prior Research & Preprints: Olaiya, R. (2026), Upstream Latent Trajectory Governance: Information Geometry, eBPF Kernel Drops, and Cryptographic Attestation for Autonomous Systems (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23677470, ORCID: 0009-0002-6809-5061) — source of the core kinematic shear equations, 0.07 / 0.19 phase boundaries, and moving-horizon baseline re-calibration principle; plus Scale-Invariant Thermodynamic Attribution preprints (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20549045, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20548469).

Prior Prototype & IP Attribution: The underlying local-first Flutter/BLE mobile prototype (Sentinel Settle, demonstrated in the project video) was developed prior to the hackathon by Thohat Ventures Ltd (underlying kinematic governance method subject to a pre-existing UKIPO patent application).

Tools & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: Built with Python (numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib), Flutter/Dart, and Microsoft Clipchamp (video assembly and .srt captions). Super Intelligence (SI) coding/documentation assistants (Cursor and Gemini) were used for data-ingestion scaffolding and documentation formatting; no NASA logos or protected branding elements were generated or modified.
